public_comment.topic: A resident noted no Selectmen or Zoning Board members appeared to be present and remarked they would only see the video and could submit questions in writing.

A participant asked whether the card-sorting exercise could be expanded online so more residents could weigh in, since turnout was low.
Participants debated whether to expand farmers market hours, with disagreement over whether the market has historically drawn enough vendors or customers.
A participant argued that improving the town green behind the library/senior center, without disturbing the existing gazebo or fire lane access, was a feasible community gathering space.

Discussion of prioritizing sidewalks and pedestrian infrastructure in commercial areas, noting MassDOT "Complete Streets" requirements are costly and space-intensive on state roads.

Discussion of traffic calming measures (speed tables) near Whalom Lake given pedestrian safety concerns for children and families.

A participant described a hypothetical inclusionary zoning scenario where a developer building a round number of apartments would have to set aside a percentage as deed-restricted affordable units, similar to what other communities require.

A card proposing a town-supported business incubator on town land was discussed, including reduced rent and shared facilities, but participants felt Brooks House repairs would likely exceed the card's stated cost/time tier.
Participants noted state (MassDOT) grant funding exists for sidewalk and Complete Streets projects, but design requirements make such projects expensive and land-intensive on state roads.

The group agreed to pause and relocate to the community room at 8:00 when the current meeting space closed for the evening.

The facilitator proposed, and the group agreed, to run the card-sorting exercise again at other public gatherings, such as the senior center, to gather broader input for the short list of recommendations.

minutes.headline: Committee ran a hands-on card-sorting workshop ranking Master Plan ideas on housing, zoning and infrastructure; no votes taken.
minutes.summary: This was an interactive public workshop for the Lunenburg Master Plan update, where a small group of attendees used a card-sorting exercise to rank draft recommendations (covering housing/zoning, economic development, facilities, and later transportation/infrastructure) by importance and urgency. No formal votes were taken; the session produced informal group consensus on which ideas seemed most important or time-sensitive, feeding into the consultants' effort to narrow a long list of recommendations to a short list for the draft Master Plan report.

what_happened.line: Attendees ranked draft Master Plan recommendations by importance and urgency in a card-sorting exercise; no votes were taken.
The group placed school facility accessibility upgrades, discussed with reference to Turkey Hill, in the highest-priority category.
The facilitator proposed repeating the exercise at other public gatherings, such as the senior center, to widen input before the short list is set.
A resident noted no Selectmen or Zoning Board members attended and turnout was described as low.

why_it_matters: This ranking exercise feeds directly into which zoning, housing and infrastructure ideas make the draft Master Plan's short list, a document that can shape future zoning and lot-size votes.
Residents who missed this session may get another chance to weigh in if the senior-center repeat happens, since the current input came from a small, self-selected group.

Ideas discussed included changes to minimum lot sizes, inclusionary zoning for new apartment development, and sidewalk/Complete Streets projects, all of which touch future town spending and zoning bylaws.
